about: Where open-field changes OS 1.7.0+0 of the OP-1 Field, and nothing else: no byte of the firmware is in this file.
stock_sha256 is the SHA-256 of the firmware file an owner copies off their own unit; every address below belongs to that one file.

patches: each place once. address and length say where it is; sum is the CRC-32 of the firmware's own bytes there, by which the loader knows the place before it changes it; name says in our words what stands there; group is the part of open-field that uses it (image: changed in the file by the builder; every other: changed in the running firmware at the start).

tables: for the loader and for each pack, which function of ours goes to which place. form: a word of data, a call, a jump, or the load of an address. room and copies: the loader copies that many bytes of the instructions the change displaces from the running firmware into the room and puts a jump back behind them. An entry has a sum of its own when its trampoline copies more bytes than the place is long.

image: what the builder changes in the firmware file itself, before anything runs. kind imm32: the number an instruction loads at that address becomes new_imm. kind call: a call of the function target, which is in the loader, over length bytes. module_base and reserved_bytes are the room for our code. entry is the address the file's first record names, and heap_fill_base and heap_fill_bytes are the file's record of zeros that the room lies in: the builder looks for all three in an owner's file before it changes anything. builder/write-manifest.mjs makes the builder's manifest from these and from a built loader. The loader is our small piece inside the firmware file; the base is the pack base.pack, a file on the unit.
The table sources in module/ are made from this file by tools/table_build.py, and docs/changes.md by tools/change_list.py.
